title: From Six Kings Slam to FIFAe finals, Saudi Arabia's events derailed by war
gist: Deadly Houthi strikes on Riyadh's airport killed 13 and wounded 300+, closing it until at least Oct. 17 and forcing Saudi Arabia to cancel or postpone flagship Vision 2030 events including an EU-Gulf summit and the FIFAe Finals.

insights.claim: Houthi strikes on Riyadh's international airport over a weekend killed 13 and wounded more than 300, the deadliest attacks in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton
insights.so_what: Direct hits on core Saudi infrastructure raise Gulf aviation and tourism risk.

insights.claim: The attacks forced the kingdom's second-biggest airport to close until at least Oct. 17.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton
insights.so_what: Watch reopening timing as a gauge of de-escalation.

insights.claim: Disruption to flagship culture, entertainment and sports events hits sectors central to Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia's program to diversify the economy away from oil.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton
insights.so_what: War risk threatens the non-oil diversification story that underpins Saudi tourism and events spending.

insights.claim: An EU-Gulf leaders' summit set for Riyadh on Oct. 24, with all 27 EU leaders due to attend, was postponed because of Houthi threats and flight suspensions, with no new date.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton
insights.so_what: Delays EU-Gulf diplomatic and trade engagement.

insights.claim: FIFA and the Saudi Esports Federation postponed the FIFAe Finals 2026, scheduled for Jeddah on Oct. 16-25.
insights.speaker: Jack Dutton
insights.so_what: Esports and sports-events investment in the kingdom faces near-term delays.
